definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese sandals woven from straw rope ({藁|わら}), secured to the foot with cords and worn directly against the bare foot or over tabi socks. The standard footwear for commoners, travelers, and soldiers in premodern Japan.

examples.japanese: {草鞋|わらじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧。
⟦{江戸時代|えどじだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{旅人|たびびと}→旅人：12725_tabibito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{草鞋|わらじ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{長|なが}い→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いた→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: Travelers in the Edo period walked long roads in straw sandals.

examples.japanese: {草鞋|わらじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{藁|わら}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{編|あ}んで→編む：00002_amu⟧⟦{作|つく}られ→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧、⟦{使|つか}い{捨|す}て→使い捨て：07665_tsukaisute⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{近|ちか}い→近い：00530_chikai⟧⟦{消耗品|しょうもうひん}→消耗品：09548_shoumouhin⟧だった。
examples.english: Waraji were woven from straw and were nearly disposable items.

notes:
Traditional footwear made from twisted straw rope. Now mainly seen in historical contexts, traditional festivals, and martial arts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {草鞋|わらじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧: to wear straw sandals
- {草鞋|わらじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱|ぬ}ぐ→脱ぐ：00518_nugu⟧: to take off straw sandals; (figuratively) to settle in at a place
- {草鞋|わらじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{編|あ}む→編む：00002_amu⟧: to weave straw sandals
- {草鞋|わらじ}{履|ば}き: wearing straw sandals

The expression {草鞋|わらじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱|ぬ}ぐ→脱ぐ：00518_nugu⟧ (lit. "to remove one's sandals") means to settle down or stop traveling — derived from the custom of removing footwear upon entering a home.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{下駄|げた}→下駄：03984_geta⟧: wooden clogs — raised wooden footwear, also traditional but distinct in material and style
- {雪駄|せった}: leather-soled sandals — more refined than waraji
